text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-After a heated late-night discussion in parliament, the cabinet withdrew municipal election bill.
-Head of Constitutional Council resigned amid heavy political pressure over appeals against the results of last year's parliamentary elections.
-President Hrawi said:"I shall use all my constitutional power to prevent postponment of the municipal elections".
-Teachers at state-run Lebanese University went on a one-day strike to protest against government's academic decisions.
-A Beirut judge indicted five suspected Japanese Red Army guerrillas on forgery charges and demanded up to 10 years jail for each.
-Argentine President Menem will visit Lebanon before the end of 1997, Minister of Emigrants Arslan said.
-Pro-Iranian Hizbollah leadership may ask for a meeting with Pope John Paul during his two-day visit to Lebanon on May 10-11.
